How the interview runs

The Microsoft SQL interview, as candidates report it

Microsoft does not publish the format. Each row is what candidates and prep guides have described publicly, with its source; where sources disagree, the row says so. Formats change — treat every specific as reported, not official.

RolesData Analyst, Data Scientist and BI roles; SQL is described as almost always tested.[2]
Data science stagesA recruiter screen of about 30 minutes, a 45-minute technical screen (SQL, statistics, ML fundamentals), then a final loop of four or five rounds of 45–60 minutes in one day.[1]
Online assessmentSources disagree. One guide describes a data science assessment on CodeSignal; another describes live coding only, with no online assessment. We could not confirm either.[3][1]
What the loop weighsA dedicated coding round (SQL and/or Python) sits beside ML, experimentation, a business case and behavioural rounds.[1]
  1. [1] Exponent — Microsoft Data Scientist interview guide (by Microsoft candidates) (updated mid-2026)
  2. [2] DataLemur — Microsoft SQL interview questions and data science guide (8 May 2025)
  3. [3] DataLemur — Microsoft data science interview guide (8 May 2025)
  4. [4] DataLemur — supercloud customer question (undated)
  5. [5] StrataScratch — Microsoft SQL interview questions (30 Oct 2023)

Sources: Exponent — Microsoft Data Scientist interview guide (by Microsoft candidates) (updated mid-2026); DataLemur — Microsoft SQL interview questions and data science guide (8 May 2025); DataLemur — Microsoft data science interview guide (8 May 2025); DataLemur — supercloud customer question (undated); StrataScratch — Microsoft SQL interview questions (30 Oct 2023). The SQL that comes up

What Microsoft SQL questions test

Reported most often, in order

  • 1Joins, including multi-table and self-joins
  • 2Aggregation with GROUP BY
  • 3Window functions (RANK vs DENSE_RANK)
  • 4CTEs and subqueries
  • 5CASE and conditional aggregation
  • 6Filtering and pattern matching

Difficulty: Mostly medium, with easy filter and concept questions mixed in. The data is product purchases and cloud product categories, app downloads by paying vs free accounts, and messaging activity.

Our Microsoft practice set, by skill

The 16 SQL Quest challenges tagged Microsoft, resolved onto the nine Skillmap skills. A challenge exercises several skills, so shares do not sum to 100%. This is the composition of the practice set on this page, not a measurement of Microsoft’s interview.

Sample questions

Microsoft SQL question shapes, and where to practise them

Shapes candidates and guides report (paraphrased)

  • Purchases by user and date: users with more than ten purchases in a single month.[2]
  • Purchases by customer and product plus a product catalogue with categories: customers who bought from every category.[4]
  • Users, paying and non-paying accounts, and daily downloads: dates on which non-paying users downloaded more than paying ones.[5]
